questions.question: Which among the following is a traditional Hindu festival centered on the Goddess Mahakali from Telangana, India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bonalu.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bonalu **is a **traditional Hindu festival **celebrated in the **Telangana region** of India, especially in the** twin cities **of **Hyderabad and Secunderabad.**
 
• The festival is celebrated in the month of** Ashada (July-August)** and is dedicated to** Goddess Mahakali,** who is believed to protect the people from diseases and **other calamities.**
 
• The festival involves the worship of **decorated pots or bonalu, **which are offered to the goddess with offerings of **rice, jaggery, curd, and other items.**
 
• The festival is also marked by **colorful processions, music, and dance** performances by women, who carry the bonalu pots on their heads and dance to the beats of drums and other instruments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dehing Patkai **is a** national park and wildlife sanctuary** located in the northeastern state of Assam, India.

 
 
• It is known for its **rich biodiversity **and is home to several rare and endangered species of flora and fauna.
 
 
 
• **Ugadi **is a traditional New Year's Day festival celebrated in the** southern states of India,** especially **Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka**.
 
 
• It marks the beginning of a new year as per the** Hindu calendar.**
 
 
 
• **Lohri **is a harvest festival celebrated in the northern states of India, especially **Punjab, Haryana, and Himachal Pradesh.**
 
 
• It is marked by **bonfires, music, and dance performances**, and the distribution of sweets and other food items

questions.question: The sepoys of Meerut arrived at the Gates of Red Fort to meet the Mughal emperor, Bahadur Shah on ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 11 May, 1857.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **sepoys of Meerut **arrived at the **Gates of Red Fort** to meet the **Mughal emperor, Bahadur Shah** on **11 May, 1857.**
 
• This event is considered as the starting point of the **Indian Rebellion of 1857**, also known as the **First War of Indian Independence.**
 
• The sepoys were led by **Mangal Pandey **who had earlier revolted against the **British East India Company.**
 
• The sepoys were protesting against the use of **animal fat **in the newly introduced** Enfield rifles, **which they had to bite off before loading the guns. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Indian Rebellion of 1857:

 
 
• The **greased cartridge incident** led to the Revolt of 1857.
 
• There was a rumor that the new Enfield rifles' cartridges were lubricated with **pig and cow fat.**
 
• The sepoys had to gnaw **off the cartridge paper **before loading these guns.
 
• **Muslims and Hindu** sepoys both objected to their use.
 
• The problematic cartridges were removed as **Lord Canning** attempted to make amends, but the harm had already been done.
 
• **Mangal Pandey,** a sepoy in Barrackpore, had resisted using the cartridge and** assaulted his superior officers** in **March 1857.**​

questions.question: Which among the following is the coldest planet in the solar system?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Uranus.'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uranus:**

 
 
• Uranus is the seventh planet from the Sun and has the coldest atmosphere in the Solar System.
 
• Its minimal temperature can drop as low as -224 degrees Celsius (-371 degrees Fahrenheit).
 
• The extreme cold is due to a combination of its distance from the Sun and its peculiar axial tilt, which causes extreme seasonal variations.
 
• Unlike other gas giants, Uranus has a lower internal heat output, contributing further to its cold temperatures.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Mars:**

 
 
• Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun and has a very thin atmosphere, leading to cold temperatures, but not nearly as cold as Uranus.
 
• Average temperatures on Mars range from -125°C (-195°F) at the poles in winter to 20°C (68°F) in the day during summer at the equator.
 
 
 
• **Neptune:**
 
 
• Neptune, the eighth planet from the Sun, is also extremely cold, but slightly warmer than Uranus due to its greater internal heat.
 
• Neptune's atmospheric temperatures can drop to around -214 degrees Celsius (-353 degrees Fahrenheit).
 
 
 
• **Saturn:**
 
 
• Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun and, while cold, it is warmer than Uranus and Neptune.
 
• Temperatures in Saturn's upper atmosphere are around -178 degrees Celsius (-288 degrees Fahrenheit).

questions.question: The settlements in which large number of houses are built very close to each other are _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Compact settlements.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Compact settlements** are characterized by a **high density of houses** built close to each other, often in a** circular or rectangular pattern.**
 
• They are typically found in** urban areas** where space is limited and **population density is high.**
 
• Compact settlements can have advantages such as efficient **land use, easy access** to **services and amenities,** and a sense of community.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other settlement types mentioned in the options include
 
 
• **star settlements, **which have a central point with houses radiating outwards;
 
• **linear settlements,** which are long and narrow and often follow a road or river; and
 
• **dispersed settlements**, which are spread out and often rural or agricultural in nature.

questions.question: Which among the following is not an alkali metals and does not belong to the Group 1 of Periodic Table?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcium.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Calcium** is **not **an alkali metal and does not belong to Group 1 of the periodic table.
 
• **Alkali metals** are **highly reactive metals** that readily lose their outermost electron to form cations with a **charge of +1.**
 
• Any of the six chemical elements in Group 1 (Ia) of the periodic table—**lithium (Li), sodium (Na), potassium (K), rubidium (Rb), cesium (Cs), and francium (Fr)**—are classified as an alkali metal.
 
• The reason the alkali metals have that name is because they react with water to produce **alkalies,** which are **powerful bases **capable of **neutralizing acids.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Calcium:**

 
 
• It is an **alkaline earth metal **that belongs to **Group 2** of the periodic table.
 
• The elements in **Group 2** of the periodic table have **two valence electrons** and are **less reactive **than alkali metals. 
 
 
 
• **Lithium:**
 
 
• A chemical element with the **atomic number 3** and the symbol **Li **is lithium.
 
• It is a **delicate, white-silver alkali metal.**
 
• It is the **least dense metal** and the least dense solid element under typical conditions.
 
 
 
• **Sodium:**
 
 
• The chemical element sodium has the atomic number **11** and the symbol **Na.**
 
• It is a** delicate, silvery-white meta**l that is exceedingly** reactive.**
 
 
 
• **Potassium:**
 
 
• The chemical element with the atomic number **19 **and the letter** K** is potassium.
 
• It is a** silvery white metal **that may be easily sliced with a knife thanks to its pliability.

questions.question: In which of the following articles, “Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion” is mentioned?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 25.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 25 **of the Indian Constitution guarantees the** freedom of conscience** and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion subject to public order, morality, and health.
 
• Nothing in this article shall affect the operation of any **existing law** or prevent the State from making any law -
 
 
• regulating or restricting any **economic, financial, political **or other **secular** activity which may be associated with religious practice;
 
• providing for **social welfare and reform** or the **throwing open of Hindu religious institutions** of a public character to all classes and sections of Hindus.
 
• The wearing and carrying of** kirpans** shall be deemed to be included in the profession of the Sikh religion.
 
• In sub-clause (b) of clause (2), the reference to Hindus shall be construed as including a reference to persons professing the** Sikh, Jaina or Buddhist religion,** and the reference to Hindu religious institutions shall be construed accordingly.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 26 **deals with the **freedom to manage religious affairs **subject to public order, morality, and health.
 
• **Article 27** prohibits the State from compelling any person to** pay taxes **for the promotion of a particular religion or religious denomination.
 
• **Article 28** prohibits the State from providing **any religious instruction** in any educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds.

questions.question: Banks are required to keep some reserves in liquid form with themselves. This is called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Statutory liquidity ratio.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statutory liquidity ratio (SLR)** is a **monetary policy tool **used by the **central bank of a country** to regulate the liquidity in the banking system.
 
• It requires banks to maintain a certain percentage of their **net demand and time liabilities (NDTL)** in the form of **liquid assets **such as **cash, gold, or government securities.**
 
• The SLR is determined by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** and is currently set at **18.00% of NDTL.**
 
• Banks have to maintain this SLR on a **daily basis **and report it to the RBI every fortnight.
 
• SLR serves as a cushion against** unforeseen liquidity shocks** in the banking system.
 
• It also ensures that banks have **enough liquid assets t**o meet the demands of their depositors.
 
• Banks cannot** lend or invest **the funds that are kept in the SLR.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Marginal stability scheme** is a facility provided by the **RBI **to banks to borrow funds in case of temporary liquidity mismatches.
 
• **Open market operations** are the buying and selling of government securities by the **RBI** to regulate the money supply in the economy.
 
• **Legal deposit ratio** is not a commonly used term in banking.

questions.question: In the Indian Judicial system, PIL stands for ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Public Interest Litigation.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **PIL** stands for **Public Interest Litigation**.
 
• It is a **legal action **initiated in a court of law for the** enforcement of public interest** or general interest in which the public or a class of the community has a **pecuniary interest **or some interest by which their legal rights or liabilities are affected.
 
• PIL is a way for the common man to **approach the courts directly** in cases of **gross violation of fundamental rights **of any person or a group of persons, especially those who are poor, ignorant or socially disadvantaged.
 
• PIL is an important tool for** ensuring social and economic justice,** and it has been used to bring about significant social reforms in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of PIL was introduced in India by** Justice P.N. Bhagwati in 1976** in the case of **Mumbai Kamgar Sabha v. Abdul Thai.**
 
• PIL is a very powerful tool as it allows any citizen or group of citizens to **approach the court directly** without the requirement of a personal interest in the case. 
 
• PIL has been used to bring about significant reforms in areas such as **environmental protection, consumer rights, human rights, and the rights of marginalized sections of society.**

questions.question: Which Mauryan ruler was called Amitrochates by the Greeks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bindusara.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mauryan ruler **who was called **Amitrochates** by the Greeks was** Bindusara.**
 
• Amitrochates means** "Slayer of Enemies" **in Greek, which shows the **military prowess** of Bindusara.
 
• Bindusara was the son of **Chandragupta Maurya**, who founded the Mauryan Empire in **321 BCE.**
 
• Bindusara expanded the Mauryan Empire by **conquering the Deccan region** and parts of South India.
 
• He was succeeded by his son, the famous **Emperor Ashoka,** who is known for his conversion to **Buddhism and promotion of non-violence.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Samudragupta **was a Gupta Emperor who ruled from **335-375 CE **and was known for his military conquests and patronage of the arts.
 
• **Kanishka** was a Kushan Emperor who ruled from **127-151 CE** and was known for his patronage of Buddhism and the arts.
 
• **Chandragupta I **was a Gupta Emperor who ruled from **320-335 CE** and was known for his military conquests and patronage of the arts.

questions.question: With respect to social groups in India, PVTGs stands for _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **PVTGs **are a **sub-category** of Scheduled Tribes in India who are considered to be the** most vulnerable** among the tribal population due to their **declining population, pre-agricultural level of technology**, and **social, economic**, and **educational backwardness.​**
 
• Primitive Tribal tribes (PTGs), the least advanced of the tribal tribes, were established as a separate category by the** Dhebar Commission in 1973**.
 
• The PTGs were renamed **Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs**) by the Indian government in **2006.**
 
• The **following criteria** are used by the Indian government to identify PVTGs. 
 
 
• technology at a pre-agricultural stage.
 
• Low literacy rate.
 
• economic sluggishness.
 
• an aging or unchanging population.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The government of India has identified** 75 PVTGs in 18 states of India**, and they are provided with **special provisions** and schemes for their development and welfare. 
 
• PVTGs are dispersed across the nation's **many geographic regions.**
 
• The PVTGs have a population of roughly** 27,68,322 **as per the **2001 Census.**
 
• The remaining groups have a population of **1000 **or fewer, with the exception of the **12 PVTGs** with a population above** 50,000.**
 
• With a** population of 4,50,217,** the PVTG of **Sahariyas** has the **highest density**, while the PVTGs of **Sentinelets and Andamanese** have extremely **low densities of 39 and 43**, respectively.
